headline: Iran Says Close to Deal with Oman, But Strait of Hormuz Remains Closed
summary: Iran says it is close to an agreement with Oman to open the Strait of Hormuz shipping route, but says this is not yet enough to fully reopen navigation. Commercial ships continue to be attacked.
why: The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important oil transit chokepoints, so disruptions there directly affect global crude and LNG supply and shipping costs.
why_moved: Continued closure and attacks on commercial ships keep supply risk elevated, while the possible Oman arrangement is not yet sufficient to restore navigation.
